Order 
This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed seeking quashment of the order dated 15.01.2010 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Gwalior in Case No.1039/2010 whereby cognizance has been taken against the petitioners for the offence under Sections 7(1), and 16 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

2. The short facts of the case are that complainant/respondent no.1 had filed a complaint before Judicial Magistrate First Class Gwalior which was registered as Case No1039/10 for convicting the petitioners alongwith others for the offences under section 7(i), 7(ii)/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 alleging that on 18.07.2009, the food inspector, complainant, intercepted truck no. MH04 GA 0439 of M/s Sherawali Roadways, Bhopal, which was allegedly carrying Ghee of various brands allegedly manufactured by different manufacturers.

The said alleged stocks were seized and kept at M/s Shiva, a Carrier Transport, Transport Nagar, Gwalior on account of absence of the owner as the driver of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24082 2 MCRC-6428-2011 truck did not produce any invoice from GCMMF ltd., Mother Dairy Gandhinagar or any of the authorized whole sale dealer / dealers of GCMMF.
It was further submitted that on 19.08.2009 at about 5:30PM, on the oral instruction of Shri Ved Prakash, ADM Gwalior, the complainant remained present at Shiva Road Carrier Transport Nagar, Gwalior.

1 S/o Stayendra Anand Age-29 years, R/o F10, Panjabi Bagh, Raisen Road Bhopal came as a representative with the authority letter of Amrit Trading Company.
Infront of them seized articles were opened and on inspection, the Jars of Amul, Sneh Gopala, Krishna Ghee Brands were found.
On the basis of suspicion, samples were taken and the proceedings of sending the sample for tests were completed.
It was further averred that the seized articles were found adulterated, which is a punishable offence, upon which tt was prayed that the respondents be punished under section 7/16 of PFA Act.
Consequently, cognizance was taken for commission of offence under Sections 7 and 16 of the PFA Act against the petitioners.

3. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners is that the petitioners are bona fide manufacturers of dairy products under the registered brand "Amul," and none of the seized articles in question were manufactured or distributed by them.

It is submitted that the seized articles were spurious and misbranded in the name of "Amul" by unauthorized persons, and the petitioners had no privity of contract with the transporter or the co-accused.

It is further urged that Rule 12-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 obliges every manufacturer, distributor or dealer selling an article of food to supply a warranty in Form VI-A or issue a cash memo or bill, but in the present case, no such document were produced by the complainant to show that the present petitioner had sold or distributed the impugned ghee to any dealer and in that process, it was being transported.
Hence, fastening of liability on the petitioners in the absence of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24082 3 MCRC-6428-2011 cogent material is wholly unsustainable in law.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that adulterated and misbranded Ghee jars were found in the truck, including those labeled as "Amul,"
and the Public Analyst's report confirmed misbranding.
The Magistrate, upon considering the complaint and documents, rightly found sufficient ground to proceed under Sections 7 and 16 of the PFA Act.
It is argued that at the stage of cognizance, a detailed appreciation of defence is not required.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record as well as impugned order.
6.

Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 prohibits manufacture for sale,
storage, distribution, or sale of adulterated or misbranded food.

Such prohibition, however,
necessarily presupposes that the person sought to be prosecuted has some nexus with the activities of manufacture, storage, distribution, or sale in respect of the adulterated or misbranded product.

Where such nexus is wholly missing and the articles in dispute are shown to be counterfeit, action against a reputed registered manufacturer whose brand name is misused by unscrupulous traders cannot be sustained.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Special Judicial Magistrate (1998) 5 SCC 749 has observed that summoning of an accused in a criminal case is a serious matter and the Magistrate must apply his judicial mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable.

sentences.text: In the present case, no material has been brought on record to demonstrate that the seized ghee was manufactured, distributed, or sold by the petitioners.
There is no warranty in Form VI-A, no cash memo, nor any invoice emanating from the petitioners.
In fact, the case of the prosecution itself is that the articles were misbranded and not genuine.

Therefore, the essential ingredients to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24082 4 MCRC-6428-2011 constitute an offence under Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 are not made out against the petitioners.
Mere misuse of the brand name "Amul" by unscrupulous traders cannot justify prosecution of the petitioners who are neither manufacturers nor suppliers of the seized adulterated articles.
Cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate without considering these vital aspects is unsustainable.
9. In view of the above discussion, the petition deserves to be allowed.
The impugned order dated 15.01.2010 passed in Case No.1039/2010 by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Gwalior insofar as it concerns the present petitioners, is hereby quashed.
10. Accordingly, the petition filed under Section 482 of CrPC is allowed and disposed of.
